prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Monthly mean ozone by monitoring station (language en).
Grid: 13 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Station" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 8: header "Jul" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Aug" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 10: header "Sep" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 11: header "Oct" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 12: header "Nov" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 13: header "Dec" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 725px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 724px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly mean ozone levels across six monitoring stations, revealing seasonal patterns and station-to-station differences.","reading":"Readers locate a station in column 1, scan horizontally across months within that row, and compare stations vertically within a given month. The month columns form one chronological analytical sequence; the station column is the row key.","groups":["Column 1 (Station): row identifier, should be visually distinct from the data field.","Columns 2–13 (Jan–Dec): one chronological sequence; can be read as quarters Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec."],"keep_intact":["Station names on one line","Month abbreviations on one line","All numeric values, including decimal points, on one line"],"may_wrap":["None; all cells are short and should remain single-line. Wrapping station names would weaken row identification and scanning."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [96, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52] · table 721×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [88, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [90, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51, 56] · table 723×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
